call: Which data is development and which is the sealed holdout
choice: Dev: EWARS monthly example + Nicaragua weekly before 2018; holdout: Laos monthly subset + Nicaragua weekly from 2018
alternatives: (a) The plan's default, holdout = one or two whole chap-core datasets with weekly development on the EWARS `example_data/`. Rejected: that weekly example has 8 periods, too short for a lagged backtest, so the weekly code path would first meet real data at the holdout. (b) A location split of the Nicaragua data. Rejected: chap backtests forecast every location jointly, and the iid spatial effect is fitted per location, so a location holdout tests a different thing from a time holdout. (c) Monthly holdout from `small_laos_data_with_polygons3.csv`. Rejected: its periods are weekly ranges, so it is not monthly.
basis: Chosen from file names, columns, row counts, location ids (no overlap with the monthly development locations) and period ranges only, before any values were looked at. The 2018 cut leaves 14 years of weekly history for development and about 5 years of held-out targets.

call: The chap backtest settings used for every R and Python evaluation
choice: n_periods 3, n_splits 7, stride 1 (chap eval's defaults); fixed in scripts/backtest_settings.env
alternatives: A longer horizon or more splits (e.g. 12 splits) for a tighter L5 estimate. Not chosen now: each split is one INLA fit under amd64 emulation, and the noise-floor runs of batch 4 multiply the cost; more splits can be added by a §4b entry if batch 5 finds the L5 comparison under-powered.
basis: chap's own defaults; n_periods equals the EWARS default prediction_periods (3), so the service is asked for its default horizon.

choice: git clone at the pinned commit, then `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --python 3.13` from that commit's uv.lock
alternatives: (a) `uv tool install chap-core --python 3.13`, as chap's setup guide says. Rejected: it installs the latest PyPI release and resolves dependencies at install time, so the platform would drift from the pinned commit. (b) `uv tool install` from the pinned clone. Rejected: still re-resolves dependencies, ignoring the lockfile.
basis: The evaluation platform is an anchor and must be pinned (plan §4); chap-core ships a lockfile at that commit.

call: Which future-weather provider chap's backtest uses
choice: `climatology`, chap's default, passed explicitly: the covariates of each forecast window are forecast per location from month/week of year, not taken from the observations
alternatives: `observed` (chap's legacy provider): the model sees the true future rainfall and temperature, which isolates the model from weather-forecast error. Not chosen: chap names climatology as the setting that reflects production, it is what chap does unless told otherwise, and R and Python see the identical covariates either way, so the fidelity comparison does not depend on the choice. A candidate perturbation for phase D.

call: What the model is given from the development files
choice: Each file reduced to the six-column chap data contract (time_period, rainfall, mean_temperature, disease_cases, population, location); rows and values copied exactly
alternatives: (a) The archived files as they are. Fails for monthly data (CH-07). (b) Drop only `month`. Rejected: the other derived columns (ID_year, E, Cases) are also used by predict.R when present and are also forecast by chap's weather provider for the future window, so they would reach the model altered too; dropping all of them is the same rule for every dataset. (c) Switch the weather provider to `observed` so the columns survive. Rejected: it changes the backtest, not the input (JC-04).
basis: The EWARS README's data contract lists the six columns, and says the derived columns are produced by predict.R's adapters, so 'callers do not need to supply them'. Diagnosis in results/diagnose_monthly/ shows the reduced monthly file runs.
matters: not yet tested; it is the condition for monthly scores existing at all

call: How the EWARS configuration is passed to chap
choice: A configuration YAML stating the EwarsConfig defaults explicitly (n_lags [3], precision 0.01, region_seasonal false, covariates rainfall + mean_temperature)
alternatives: No YAML, letting the service apply its own defaults. Equivalent in effect at this commit, but leaves the configuration implicit, and the batch-4 config variants need the YAML route anyway, where an omitted covariate list silently means none (CH-08).

choice: chap-core's three built-in models with role `baseline`: global_median, seasonal_median, persistence (`builtin:<name>`)
alternatives: NaiveEstimator (`naive_model`, a Poisson draw around the per-location mean) and the scikit-learn Poisson regressors in chap_core/predictor/. Not run: chap's docs describe them as test stand-ins, not as baselines; the REST API runs exactly the three role-baseline models on every backtest.

call: Which R reference image is run
choice: The CI-built GHCR image tag sha-964eea8, pinned by digest sha256:959fb4f0…c6ff88; the run checks that /api/v1/info reports git_revision 964eea8b…
alternatives: A local build from the pinned clone. Not needed: the plan asks for it only if the digest cannot be tied to the pinned commit, and the publish workflow's sha tag plus the reported git_revision tie it.
